notes: Perfect claim overlap (C4, C26, C40, C41, C42, C97) regarding 20% basal body length variation. LLM accepts MRA classification as robust, while peer reviewers question whether mask-dependent structural differences indicate over-alignment artifacts that undermine the flexibility measurements.

Perfect claim overlap (C7, C8, C44-C48, C50, C119, C120, C125, C127) on YscD elasticity. Both agree these claims are well-supported. Crystal structure and MD simulations are independent of sub-tomogram averaging concerns, so peer reviewers accept these findings.

Perfect claim overlap (C9, C54, C55, C58, C101) on YscC stretching 30-40%. LLM accepts isolated liposome structure as valid reference. Peer reviewers specifically flag YscC liposome structure (Figure 6B) as particular concern for over-alignment artifacts, making comparative measurements uncertain.

Perfect claim overlap (C74, C107, C108, C109) on osmotic stress experiments. Both agree these experimental observations of basal body elongation under high salt conditions support the elasticity hypothesis and are independent of structural averaging concerns.

Perfect claim overlap (C10, C73, C85) on generalization to other two-membrane complexes. Both find this hypothesis uncertain, though for slightly different reasons: LLM notes lack of direct validation in other systems; peer reviewers note dependence on structural measurements that require validation.

High claim overlap (C27, C51-C53, C69, C70, C130, C131, C133, C135) on pseudo-atomic YscDJ ring model and 24-mer stoichiometry. LLM accepts model fitting to cryo-EM density. Peer reviewers question reliability of models fitted to potentially artifact-containing density maps until structural data is validated.

Partial overlap (C2, C3, C86 shared; peer includes C5, C6, C28-C35, C87, C88, C105, C106). LLM accepts first in situ structural determination as well-supported. Peer reviewers express concern about over-alignment artifacts, disconnected/inverted densities, requiring validation through independent half-dataset alignment before accepting structural claims.

Minimal overlap (C6, C30 shared; LLM includes C56, C61, C62, C64, C100, C104). LLM accepts that in situ structures are ~40% longer than isolated structures with CEMOVIS validation. Peer reviewers' concerns about over-alignment artifacts in structural averaging affect reliability of these comparative length measurements.

Minimal overlap (C5, C87, C88 shared). LLM accepts structural conservation between Y. enterocolitica and S. flexneri despite lower S. flexneri resolution. Peer reviewers' general concerns about structural averaging reliability affect confidence in comparative structural claims.

Partial overlap (C89, C90 shared; LLM includes C91-C93; peer includes C38, C39). Both uncertain about export gate positioning differences and YscV assignments. LLM notes unclear functional significance; peer reviewers note YscV position interpretation requires validation tests to rule out artifacts.
